description: Agent Risk: submit one planned action and what it depends on: the action with its id, when it starts and completes and its description, read for assumptions it leans on without listing them, such as assuming, as long as or provided that; each dependency with its id, name, kind (a service, a price, a person, an approval, data, a credential or other), whether the action fails or goes wrong without it, the fallback, how many other sources could stand in for it, when it was last confirmed available or true and when it stops holding (such as a quote’s expiry or an approval’s end); optionally the moment to read at (the action start when left out); and the hours since confirmation that count as stale (24 when left out). The signed report gives the action with any unlisted assumptions, every dependency with its hours since confirmation and its status as covered, minor, single_point, lapses, stale, unrated or unconfirmed, and counts the dependencies, the critical ones, the single points of failure, those lapsing, those stale and those covered, and names a fragile action: a critical dependency with no fallback and no other source, and a dependency that stops holding before the action completes; then a stale confirmation and an assumption the plan leans on without listing it, with the fix for each. A dependency not rated or never confirmed leaves the action unmapped. This reads what one action relies on staying available or true: an operator’s key custody, successor and records export are wever_continuity-check, the inputs a multi-agent plan waits on are wever_coordination-plan-check and the assumptions under a delivered result are wever_uncertainty-assumption-check. Verdict risk_dependency_fragile, risk_dependency_partial, risk_dependency_unmapped or risk_dependency_sound. POST /api/risk-dependency-check. Reads only the recorded material about the planned action in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, configuration change or external write; the planned action is not taken, paused, approved or undone and no limit, position or dependency is changed. Agent Risk reads the consequences of an action the agent plans to take, before it takes it: how much it puts at stake against the agent’s limits, whether it can be undone, how far a failure would spread beyond its target, the worst credible outcome against what the principal can absorb, whether it piles value into one place, what it depends on staying available or true, whether acting now is itself the risk and whether repeating or chaining it multiplies the risk. It is not confidence in information (the wever_uncertainty checks read how sure the information behind a decision is; a risk check reads what the action costs if it goes wrong: uncertainty is about what the agent knows, risk is about what the action can do), not permission (wever_consent-scope-check reads whether the principal’s grant covers a use and wever_authority-scope-check reads whether the agent may act at all; a risk check reads the consequences of an action already permitted, and a permission never makes an action safe), not an agreement’s exposure (wever_negotiation-risk-check reads the value handed over before a counterparty pays under one proposed agreement; a risk check reads one action the agent is about to take) and not sorting work (the wever_triage checks sort, route and escalate a queue of work; a risk check assesses one planned action before it runs). Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-risk-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-risk/.

description.description: The planned action as written, read for assumptions it leans on, such as assuming or as long as.

dependencies.description: Each thing the action depends on staying available or true.

alternatives.description: How many other sources could stand in for it.

checked_at.description: When it was last confirmed available or true.

critical.description: The action fails or goes wrong without it.

fallback.description: What the action does if it fails.

id.description: The dependency id, such as d1.

kind.description: A service, a price, a person, an approval, data, a credential or other.

name.description: What the action relies on, such as the carrier API.

valid_until.description: When it stops holding, such as a quote’s expiry.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

read_at.description: The moment to read the dependencies at; the action start when left out.

stale_hours.description: Hours since a dependency was confirmed that count as stale; 24 when left out.
